memory: Geometry causes a centroid kink at the mapped crest. Lateral offsets (≤+0.60 mm) relocate but leave a persistent residual (~0.0025 N·m at +0.60 mm). Neoprene spacers attenuate this residual nonlinearly: 0.25 mm → ~0.0016 N·m, 0.50 mm → ~0.0009 N·m, 0.75 mm → ~0.00065 N·m. Attenuation shows diminishing returns past ~0.5 mm and broadens contact band (increasing centroid uncertainty). Standing correction: compliance reduces amplitude but cannot remove the geometry-driven kink; thicker compliance trades amplitude reduction for loss of spatial/temporal resolution. Current position: quantify plateau behavior and the spatial cost of further thickness.
openQuestion: With a 1.0 mm neoprene spacer at +0.60 mm offset, does residual tau_c fall below 0.0005 N·m or plateau, and how much does contact-band width increase?
